open_points.subject: Linux host requirement and O_NOFOLLOW premise
open_points.text: A release runs on Linux and on no other host, of any version that runs the sandbox runtime, which the start proves (A03); owner, 2026-10-18). / A20 rule 3 ... no module owns them / surface.serve_kernel runs the start in this order: installation.load_installation; bindings.check_installed_instances; store.open_store; sandbox.probe_sandbox
open_points.question: Which module owns proving the Linux-host prerequisite, and how may installation and store rely on it for unconditional O_NOFOLLOW use when both run before sandbox.probe_sandbox, the stated proof, and A20 rule 3 has no runtime owner?
options: The release artifact guarantees Linux before the process starts, so no runtime module checks it
sandbox.probe_sandbox owns the proof and must run before installation and store
installation or surface performs an earlier explicit Linux-host check
open_points.default_guess: Treat Linux as a release/platform guarantee established before process start, with installation and store unconditionally using O_NOFOLLOW.
